<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Reported 2026-10-26 by the osk-central prime (report: ~/osk/osk_central-governance/.harness/government/reports/2026-10-26-codex-spawn-defect.md, pij-fleet#76). On main 26fc3ba with codex-cli 0.164.0: (1) `pij-rs spawn --harness codex` times out waiting for registration (30s and 120s) in three governments although the Codex TUI is healthy; earlier seats stayed session null and needed a trust prompt answered. (2) Replies sent with `pij send` from Codex seats are attributed to other seats (two reviewers both arrived as one seat; another arrived as a parentless seat). Plan 177 (#66) recently changed Codex footer parsing, so the cause may be new, old, or in Codex itself: this plan diagnoses before it fixes. Rulings: assets/rulings.md.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- A Codex seat spawned by pij binds, or fails with an error that says why.
- A Codex seat's messages carry its own id, or refuse.
- Every fix rests on a captured, reproduced cause.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Supporting Codex versions other than 0.164.
- Changing tmux capture or control mode (PR #73 owns that).
- Claude, Copilot, OMP or Pi bind paths.
- Fixing #65 generally beyond what Codex identity needs.

| ac-0007 | Cost (R12). The Codex binder is a daemon loop that launches nothing per tick per seat. A tick reads the Codex thread-lock directory and the roster in-process and does nothing else unless a Codex thread started since the last tick or a pending spawned Codex row appeared; it is idle when no pending spawned Codex row exists. Then each pending row costs at most one process-file read (in-process on Linux, one /usr/sbin/lsof on macOS), and a bind costs one tmux call and one ps. Launches scale with Codex thread starts times pending rows, never with the tick interval. Tests count launches on an injected port; a live spawn-rate reading is taken before merge and after deploy. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0004](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | [lg-0009](assets/execution-log.dd.md#entries) |
